title: Solar Energy Ordinance Extraction Schema
description:
Regulatory requirements for solar photovoltaic energy generation facilities. SCOPE: utility-scale solar farms, commercial solar installations, ground-mounted solar arrays, solar energy overlay districts, and solar energy generation facilities. EXCLUDE: wind energy, geothermal energy, biomass, battery storage, and other non-solar technologies unless a requirement explicitly applies to solar within the cited section. ALSO EXCLUDE: small residential rooftop solar exemptions unless the document regulates commercial or utility-scale solar. CRITICAL FILTERING: only extract provisions that explicitly mention solar, photovoltaic, PV, solar panels, solar arrays, solar facilities, or clearly apply to solar in context.

Every requirement row is decomposed on four axes: WHAT is regulated (feature + specific_subject + requirement_description + applies_to), HOW MUCH (value + value_category + value_interpretation + units + range_low/range_high), HOW BINDING (obligation), and WHEN/WHERE (condition + applies_to). Evidence lives in source_verbatim, reasoning, and section.

document_applicability.description: Scope verification and filtering transparency for solar ordinances.

applies_to_solar.description: Set to true only if the document contains provisions regulating utility-scale or commercial solar facilities. Set to false if it only covers other technologies or only small residential solar exemptions.

extraction_approach.description: Document which sections were extracted and which sections were excluded. If the document is a zoning code that lists solar as a permitted or conditional use in certain zones, extract only the solar use classification and the zone-specific standards that clearly apply to solar. Use format: 'Extracted [sections]; Excluded [sections]'.
examples: Extracted Section 30 Solar Energy Overlay District; Excluded battery-storage CUP references and general zoning text not specific to solar.
Extracted definitions and zoning-district permissions for Solar Energy Farm; Excluded private-road and non-solar definitions.

relevant_sections.description: Solar-related sections cited exactly as written. Null if none.

jurisdiction.description: Geographic and regulatory context for the ordinance.

state.description: State name exactly as written in the document.

county.description: County name exactly as written, keeping the County suffix if present. For municipal ordinances, use the governing county if it is explicit in the document.

subdivision.description: City, township, or other subdivision if the ordinance applies below the county level. Null if county-wide or not applicable.

jurisdiction_type.description: Jurisdiction type exactly as stated, such as County, City, Township, Town, Village, or Borough.

year.description: Most relevant ordinance year, typically adoption, amendment, or effective year. Use a four-digit integer when determinable.

source.description: URL or document reference for the source ordinance. Use the SOURCE_URL from the CONTEXT block at the top of the document if present. Null if not available.

requirements.description: Regulatory requirements applicable to solar facilities. EXTRACTION RULES: (1) Split one regulation into separate rows when it covers different features, different facility types, or different dimensional subjects; distinguish them with 'specific_subject'. (2) Create separate rows for participating and non-participating setbacks only if the ordinance distinguishes them. (3) Extract tiered values as separate rows with value_interpretation='tiered' and the triggering band in 'condition'. (4) For a set of interchangeable allowed values (e.g., permitted district codes), use a single row with value_interpretation='enumerated' and populate applicable_values instead of repeating rows. (5) FACILITY SCOPE vs TRIGGER: put the governed facility type in 'applies_to' (e.g., 'Solar Energy Farm'); put the situational circumstance in 'condition' (e.g., 'for facilities exceeding 25 MW'). Never mix the two. (6) MIXED CLAUSES: when one clause contains both a measurable threshold and a non-numeric prohibition/exception, emit separate rows by semantic role (quantitative row for value/units/value_interpretation; qualitative row for non-numeric prohibition/exception). (7) Do not create placeholder rows for topics the ordinance does not address. (8) Keep non-solar technologies out unless the solar section explicitly cross-references them in a way that changes the solar requirement.

feature.description: Standardized solar requirement feature name (the WHAT axis) used for cross-jurisdiction comparison.

specific_subject.description: Specific dimensional or contextual subject within the feature (WHAT axis). Participates in the dedup key. Examples: total area, minimum width, minimum depth, screening height, timeline for removal, financial security amount, from centerline, or from right-of-way edge. Use null when the feature itself is already specific enough.

applies_to.description: Solar facility type or scope the requirement governs (WHAT/WHERE axis). Use the ordinance's own terminology when practical. This is NOT the situational trigger (use 'condition') and NOT the obligation.

requirement_description.description: Clean, obligation-free description of the regulated action or object (WHAT axis). NEVER include obligation language — no 'required', 'shall', 'may', 'must', 'prohibited'. Used for qualitative requirements; null for purely quantitative rows.

value_category.description: REQUIRED. How this requirement's value should be interpreted (HOW MUCH axis). 'quantitative' = a measurable magnitude lives in 'value' (distance, dBA, acres, MW, %, $). 'qualitative' = there is no magnitude; the substance lives in 'requirement_description' (or an enumerated set in applicable_values) and 'value' should be null. Independent of 'obligation': a quantitative limit can be conditional and a qualitative item can be required.

value.description: For quantitative requirements, the numeric magnitude ONLY (e.g., 500, 20, 55). Use a range string (e.g., '100-500') when the provision states a span, set value_interpretation='range', and populate range_low/range_high. For qualitative or enumerated requirements set value to null and use requirement_description or applicable_values. NEVER embed units or obligation words ('required', 'may', 'shall', 'prohibited') in value.

value_interpretation.description: How the value is bounded or structured (HOW MUCH axis). 'exact' = single fixed value ('shall be 35 feet'); 'minimum' = floor ('at least', 'no less than'); 'maximum' = ceiling ('shall not exceed'); 'range' = a span — populate range_low and range_high; 'formula' = computed ('1.1x panel height'); 'tiered' = value depends on a band — emit one row per tier; 'enumerated' = a discrete set of allowed values (e.g., permitted district codes) — pair with applicable_values. Null for qualitative requirements (present/absent).

units.description: Unit of measurement written in full words when possible. Use null for zoning districts, yes/no requirements, formulas without a unit, or pure text values.

range_low.description: Lower bound of the span when 'value' is a range (e.g., 100 for '100-500'). Domain-agnostic: works for distances, dBA, MW, acres, etc. Null unless value_interpretation='range'.

range_high.description: Upper bound of the span when 'value' is a range (e.g., 500 for '100-500'). Domain-agnostic: works for distances, dBA, MW, acres, etc. Null unless value_interpretation='range'.

obligation.description:
REQUIRED. How binding the requirement is (HOW BINDING axis). Never place obligation language inside 'value' or 'requirement_description'.

Normalization rules:
- Quantitative limits/setbacks/windows should use obligation='required'; encode direction in value_interpretation (minimum/maximum/range) even when wording is negative (e.g., 'shall not exceed', 'shall not be within').
- Reserve obligation='prohibited' for qualitative bans with no measurable threshold.
- For permit-gated phrasing ('may be permitted only through ... permit'), encode the permit gate as obligation='required' on the approval row.

- 'required': mandatory — 'shall', 'must', 'is required', 'no less than'.
- 'prohibited': forbidden qualitative bans — 'shall not', 'no person shall', 'may not', 'is not permitted', 'prohibited'.
- 'conditional': discretionary authority — 'may require', 'at the discretion of', 'as a condition of approval', 'unless waived'.
- 'allowed': explicitly permitted with no mandate — 'is permitted', 'may be located', 'is allowed'.
- 'recommended': non-binding advisory — 'should', 'encouraged', 'best available technology'.
- 'informational': definitions, procedures, measured baselines, or referenced external standards with no direct obligation.

When multiple verbs appear, precedence: prohibited > required > conditional > recommended > allowed > informational. Cite the trigger language in 'reasoning'.

condition.description: Situational trigger or circumstance that governs WHEN or WHERE the requirement applies (WHEN/WHERE axis). This is the condition/circumstance, NOT the facility type (use 'applies_to') and NOT the obligation. Null if the requirement applies unconditionally.
examples: when multiple lots are included in the district

applicable_values.description: Parallel interchangeable atomic values that share an IDENTICAL obligation, condition, and evidence. Use ONLY when (a) the values are categorical/enumerated (e.g., permitted zoning district codes, acceptable permit types) and (b) all share the same obligation + condition + source. Replaces solar's former 'alternative_option'. Pair with value_interpretation='enumerated'. Null when a single value applies.

source_verbatim.description: Exact operative clause copied word-for-word from the ordinance (EVIDENCE axis). Never paraphrase — this is the audit anchor. If the passage exceeds 50 words, quote the operative head, insert '…', then the tail. Null only if no single passage can be quoted.
examples: Area within each SEOD must be a minimum of 20 acres.
Solar Energy Farms are only permitted within the AG zoning district under an approved Interim Use Permit.
A SEOD must be at least 2640 feet from another SEOD.

reasoning.description: Terse 'trigger → label' rationale (EVIDENCE axis), <=15 words, citing the governing verb and the value_category decision. Goes in ignore_fields and is hidden from compiled output. Null if self-evident.
examples: 'must be a minimum of' → required; number → quantitative/minimum

section.description: Ordinance section/article reference (EVIDENCE axis), cited exactly as written (e.g., 'Section 30-4', 'Article XII § 5').

notes.description: Optional analyst note for nuance, exceptions, or cross-references that help interpret the extracted value.
